items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Abbey's combo was the band that had to accompany a big revue... I was asking forty dollars a week and I really earned my pay.

ctx.x: type American musicians in Paris at that time, I didn't try too hard to learn the language. Sometimes when I wanted to take a taxi home, I would have to ask three or four drivers before I could find one that understood me. And I would say the name of the street to him the same as I had said it to the others and by luck he would understand. But it was one of those things that if a foreigner didn't or couldn't pronounce a word with a certain accent, the taxi driver would not try to understand.

Willie started working at Chez Florence again and not long after we had opened, a violin player named Leon Abbey contacted me and asked me if I would like to go to India with him. I had heard about Leon Abbey in New York because he was the leader of an orchestra that came to Europe a few months before I arrived in the big city and had taken Fletcher Allen, an alto sax player with him. Fletcher had played with Lloyd Scott before I joined the band and the Scott Brothers used to talk about him often. Leon Abbey and…

This offer to go to India really excited me. The conditions were 50 dollars a week, room and board and transportation from Paris to Bombay and back to Paris. I would have to pay Beezie's transportation and board but that was a small matter as far as I was concerned. The excitement of going to India was all that mattered to me. Other things I would take [them] in their stride.
